$$\therefore\ X = 44 \text{ cents}$$

Cameron is a teacher and his gross annual income is \$108 000. He paid a total of \$26 200 in Pay As You Go (PAYG) tax during the 2022–23 financial year. solutions.latex:
Deductions are subtracted from gross income.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Taxable income}&=108\,000-(342+674)\\&=\$106\,984\end{aligned}$$
This income lies in the bracket above \$45 000, so
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Tax payable}&=5902+(106\,984-45\,000)\times 0.325\\&=\$26\,046.80\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Total taxes}&=26\,046.80+2139.68\\&=\$28\,186.48\end{aligned}$$
Cameron has paid \$26 200, which is less than \$28 186.48.
$$\therefore\ \text{Cameron owes the ATO } \$1986.48.$$
criteria: Correct answer
Finds the total tax including the Medicare levy, or equivalent merit
Finds the tax payable on the taxable income, or equivalent merit
Finds the taxable income, or equivalent merit

Amanda has a total income of \$118 000. Her tax payable is \$27 750.

What is Amanda's taxable income, correct to the nearest dollar?

solutions.latex:
Her taxable income $x$ lies in the bracket starting at $\$45\,000$, so the tax is $5092 + 0.325(x - 45\,000)$.
$$\begin{aligned} 27\,750 &= 5092 + 0.325(x - 45\,000) \\ \dfrac{27\,750 - 5092}{0.325} &= x - 45\,000 \\ x &= 69\,716.92308 + 45\,000 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Taxable income} \approx \$114\,717$$
criteria: Correct answer
Correct substitution in the correct formula, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Source wrote $114 716.92; the question asks for nearest dollar, so final line rounded to $114 717 (same value). The tax table is not visible here, so the bracket used is taken from the source.
